statement: For every connected admissible surface and every homeomorphism operator subgroup with a dense orbit, inclusion of its centralizer induces an injection from the centralizer fundamental group to the operator-invariant ambient fundamental group. On hyperbolic surfaces the identity-component centralizer therefore has trivial fundamental group. Neither operator local compactness nor locally compact loop-generated closure is assumed.
depends_on: C28 loop-generated orbit classification; C30 exact operator restriction and free proper closed image; C33 Lie structure of that proper image; C34 global contraction without open loop-generated orbits; C37 global continuity on the closure of all dimension-two proper-image open orbits; C39 explicit ambient disk lifting and inverse lifting
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b) infinite-operator request; exact centralizer inclusion on fundamental groups for a dense operator orbit
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Every required passage between orbit actions and covering actions is given by an actual restriction, orbit equality, or covering map.
notes: Commutation gives h(Gx)=G(hx). The union of open G-orbits is H-invariant; if nonempty it contains the dense H-orbit and is dense. In each open orbit O, a point y from that dense orbit satisfies H y intersect O equals H_O y. The closure Q_O of the actual restriction image acts freely and properly, so its closed orbit containing this dense subset is all O. Hence every open G-orbit has dimension-two proper operator image and C37 applies on the entire plane. With no open G-orbits C34 applies instead. For an arbitrary admissible surface, the ambient filling lifts by the actual map from D2 times its universal cover; deck-valued commutators remain the identity, and the full operator lift orbit equals the full inverse image of the original dense orbit. The plane contraction therefore descends with exact operator equivariance and jointly continuous inverses. General operator actions without a dense orbit remain part of Open C12.
